en: Now, obviously, when building web servers,
you often wanna do more than just send back
this basic text here. You may, for example,
be interested in the request that was
received to
do different things based on which request
you received. So it's quite handy that this
fetch method automatically receives a
request object and that request object is of
type Request, which just like Response is a
standard web API, which again could be used
in the browser. And here you would typically
construct it in the browser On the server,
we instead get it and Bun gives it to us
automatically. So this native Bun serve API
uses these official web APIs like response
and request for the data exchange, for
handling the request and constructing the
response. That's pretty neat about Bun.
Now, what can we use the request for? For
example, to extract data like the URL.
That URL will be a string, but we can
extract useful information out of it by
constructing a URL object by wrapping it
with this URL constructor or class here,
which again is a web standard. URL is
another web API that can be used to
construct URL objects, for example, based on
URL strings. And why would we do that? Well,
because now we can extract some useful
information from that URL
in an easier way. Stuff like the host or the
protocol that was used, HTTP versus HTTPS,
for example,
or the pathname. So the part after the
domain.
So in academind.com/courses,
/courses would be the pathname. Now, why
would we do that? Well, because now we can
check if path is equal to slash, for
example, which is the root path for just the
domain slash nothing, no matter if the slash
is entered or not for this specific case.
And then we could send back different
responses for different paths. So for a
courses path, we could send back a different
response than for this standard path here.
So we can grab this
response, copy it, paste it in there
and say
hello world, what we did before.
Then for courses, I could say
join my courses.
And then here, if we make it past these if
checks, we could send back a fallback. Like
NotFound and maybe here we also want to set
a status code of 404 to send back a proper
404 response. The default if you don't set
it is 200.
So with that, we now have our own basic
routing implemented in this fetch method.
So with that, if I restart that server and
we have to do that since we made some
changes, to make sure we don't have to do
that again and again, we can
add the watch flag here.
This will watch the code and restart the
server automatically if we change the code.
But with that added and the server
restarted, if I reload, I still see Hello
World.
If I enter /courses here, I see Join My
Courses, which indeed is a good idea.
And if I enter something else, I get Not
Found.
And in that case, if I open the developer
tools and go to the Network tab, you'll see
that if I reload, I do indeed get the 404
status code.
So that's basic routing implemented with
Bun, with the default standard Bun server.
